obtained.how: the published article's PDF in the University of Konstanz's institutional repository (KOPS), open access

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the title page ('Limnol. Oceanogr., 50(6), 2005, 2008–2021'; 15 authors, Gyllström first)
bibliography.note: 'Gyllström, M. et al.' is acceptable; the co-authors are Hansson, Jeppesen, García-Criado, Gross, Irvine, Kairesalo, Kornijow, Miracle, Nykänen, Nõges, Romo, Stephen, Van Donk and Moss

claims.claim: across 81 shallow European lakes zooplankton tracked TP
claims.location: p. 2009 (PDF p. 2), abstract; p. 2013 (PDF p. 6), Table 3
claims.quote: the most important predictor of zooplankton biomass and community structure
claims.conditions: 81 lakes of mean depth < 4 m (0.4–3.9 m), 38–68° N; summer sampling 2000–2001; multiple regression of log total zooplankton dry biomass on log TP, climate, plant volume infested and area
claims.note: log10 ZOO = 0.71 + 0.88 log10 TP − 0.20 CLIM + 0.38 PVI (r² 0.49, n 65), read on the page image of Table 3

claims.claim: benthic and plant-associated taxa were 'typically almost half' of the zooplankton biomass in shallow lakes
claims.quote: Benthic and plant-associated taxa (typically almost half the total zooplankton biomass)
claims.conditions: biomass (dry weight) of whole-lake samples pooled from a shore-to-centre transect; the group includes littoral cladocerans and littoral rotifers (Table 2)

claims.claim: summer crustacean zooplankton 45–100 µg/L in mesotrophic lakes (Gyllström 2005)
claims.source_value: the paper gives no crustacean biomass for mesotrophic lakes; the digits match its regression for TOTAL zooplankton (rotifers included), log10 ZOO = 0.71 + 0.88 log10 TP, evaluated at TP ≈ 12–30 µg/L with the climate and plant terms set to zero (≈ 46–102 µg DW/L; project arithmetic). Measured total biomass across the 81 lakes: 4.7–5,161 µg DW/L, mean 477, median 289, at median TP 55 µg/L
claims.location: p. 2013 (PDF p. 6), Table 3 (ZOO row); p. 2010 (PDF p. 3), Table 1
claims.conditions: dry weight; total zooplankton including rotifers; shallow (< 4 m mean depth) European lakes; CLIM is a PCA score (positive = warmer), PVI the arcsine-square-root plant volume
claims.note: cite it as 'total zooplankton, rotifers included, from Gyllström et al.'s TP regression (project arithmetic)'; for a cold-climate lake the negative CLIM score raises the prediction a little

claims.claim: the chydorids are up to half the zooplankton of weedy shallows (Gyllström et al. 2005)
claims.source_value: benthic and plant-associated taxa as a group — littoral cladocerans (Eurycercus, Camptocercus, Acroperus, Alonopsis, Simocephalus, Chydorus spp., Graptoleberis, Pleuroxus, Rhynchotalona, Disparalona, Scapholeberis, Sida, Ophryoxus) plus littoral rotifers — were 'typically almost half' of whole-lake zooplankton biomass; Chydorus sphaericus itself is classed as pelagic
claims.location: p. 2009 (PDF p. 2), abstract; p. 2012 (PDF p. 5), Table 2; p. 2011 (PDF p. 4), Methods (sampling)
claims.quote: along a transect running from the shore to the center of the lake
claims.conditions: samples pooled from 5–10 points along a shore-to-centre transect, not from weed beds
claims.note: three differences: 'typically almost half', not 'up to half'; the whole littoral group (crustaceans and rotifers), not chydorids alone; whole-lake pooled samples, not the weedy shallows. Their biomass was predicted mainly by plant cover (PVI)

notes: Paper §3.3.4's use is right. The two code comments need rewording (config.js:1361 and :1580). Useful for the rewrite: Fig. 4 (p. 2016) shows large pelagic zooplankton medians of roughly 30 µg DW/L at TP 0–25 µg/L and ~100 at 25–50, and small pelagic roughly 20 and 100 (read from the boxplots; approximate); carbon converted to dry weight × 2.2; 'ice' lakes (≥ 4 months ice) responded differently to TP — Hot Brook would be an ice lake.
